messages:
Ravi: Quick sync — how do we want the Console to surface 'degradation noise' during automatic fallback rollouts? Concern: transient spikes (5xx / p95 latency blips) look like failures in the UI and trigger support noise. Need ideas for UX and telemetry knobs.
Ana: I like separating 'policy action' vs 'signal noise' visually. show the fallback decision (why it fired) and a small noise meter so users know it's noisy vs sustained.
Maya: Agree. Mock idea: two-state banner — "Fallback active (temporary)" with an inline badge: "noise: 23% (5m)". And a hover tooltip that explains sampling and retention.
Ben: Product ask: can we link the banner to the exact rollouts/eval set that caused the decision? folks want to playback the prompt set that tripped it.
Chloe: Ops: also need to show sampling rate and persisted traces. If we only surface aggregated noise, we still need a quick path to raw events (sampled IDs) for forensics.
Ana: UX idea: collapse view by default — summary line + small sparkline. expand to show triggers: counts of 5xx, timeout, p95, and last decision id.
Maya: example layout: [Banner] [Sparkline] [Why: throttling-policy v3 -> switched to model-x-small] [Inspect] button. Inspect opens modal with samples + exact request/response (sanitized).
Ravi: Nice. What about the threshold wording? ppl panic when they see "fallback engaged". Maybe language: "service degraded — protective mode enabled" vs "fallback engaged"?
Ben: Wording matters. Suggest: "Protective routing active — degrading to conserve latency while we surface errors". Also require a timestamp & duration.
Chloe: Telemetry: add an event "fallback.initiated.preview" whenever the policy flips because of short-lived noise. Give it meta: trigger_type, window_size, sample_rate.
Ravi: Can we keep the default sampling low but persist 1 in N decisions for 7 days? we want replayability without huge DB cost.
Chloe: yes — default inspect_rate=0.02, persist_events: 1 in 100 of sampled decisions. configurable per policy.
Maya: UX should surface sampling controls inline (small link: "Sampling: 2% — change"). Changing should open a quick-settings flyout (no full navigation).
Ana: Also add a quick 'mark as expected' toggle so product teams can annotate that this noise is acceptable during a rollout. That should suppress alerts + SLA noise.
Ben: Related: provide a 'replay' button that runs sampled requests against both primary and fallback models in a sandbox and shows diff of outputs (side-by-side). Helps judge quality impact.
Ravi: Love the replay idea. Quick technical sketch for telemetry payload (for the backend team):
```json
{"policy":"auto-fallback","trigger":"p95>800","window":"5m","inspect_rate":0.02,"persist_sample":0.01,"decision_id":"d_20250315_1422"}
```
Ana: Nice. UI question: should we aggregate noise per route, per model, or per rollout? We'd probably want all three levels.
Chloe: we can compute hierarchies server-side. consider adding a 'noise attribution' table: route -> model -> region -> percentage.
Maya: Visual affordance: small color ramp (green -> amber -> red) but add pattern-fill for 'noisy but transient' so color alone doesn't alarm.
DevBot: DeployBot: Canary: auto-fallback policy v3 deployed to staging at 1751239999. :rocket:
Ravi: OK next steps: Ana + Maya pair on banner mock; Chloe + eng infra define minimal telemetry schema (inspect_rate, persist_events, attribution); Ben to spec replay API; I'll draft small doc for default wording and samples. Anyone object?
Ben: no objections, will write API contract.
Maya: will drop 2 mock variants by EOD.
Ana: will add accessibility notes + microcopy.
Chloe: will list retention/quotas for persisted samples.
Ravi: thanks all. :thumbsup:
